In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Dabbahu is an active composite volcano with a remarkably diverse range of magma types, and a relatively simple plumbing system.
the magmatic evolution of Dabbahu was dominated by the fractionation and mixing of basaltic and rhyolitic magmas, with the former being the most voluminous.
Dabbahu is an excellent natural laboratory for the study of magmatic processes in a rift setting.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Dabbahu is not a simple composite cone but a complex, composite, polygenetic, and polyplutonic volcano that erupted a wide range of magma types over a relatively short period of geologic time.
Dabbahu is an active, but relatively small composite volcano that is erupting a remarkably diverse suite of lavas.
Dabbahu is the first well-studied example of a composite volcano in a continental rift, and the first well-studies example of a composite rhyolitic volcano.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Dabbahu is an example of a composite volcano in which a diverse suite of magmas was erupted from a single vent system over a short period of time, probably in the range of 10 to 20 k.y. The
